purpose: Answers one question in one command: is the deployed Site running this revision, or an older one? Merging to main does not update the Site, so the repository and the Site drift apart silently, and every symptom of that drift looks like a product defect. Each marker is a short string this revision renders (or has stopped rendering) on a public page, chosen so that its absence on the deployed origin proves the Site is behind rather than merely unconfigured.

markers.reason: The source currency section renders unconditionally from a bundled record, so a deployment carrying it cannot hide it and a deployment without it cannot fake it.
The French half of the same section, so a half-built bilingual deployment is caught as well.

markers.reason: The owner retired this banner. A deployment still showing it is older than that decision, which makes a retired string a sharper staleness signal than any added one.

The cumulative headline is the landing page's largest figure and renders from bundled span measurements with nothing gating it, so a deployment that answers /en without this heading is serving the landing page as it stood before the 2026-09-20 redesign.
The French half of the same headline, so a deployment that rebuilt one locale and not the other is caught on the landing page as well as on the data and explore pages.

The 2026-09-20 redesign replaced this landing section with the evidence marks block. A page still carrying its heading is older than that work, and a retired string catches a deployment that kept something this revision removed, which no added string can do.

gatedSurfacesReason: These surfaces are hidden when their worker bindings are absent, so their absence is the correct fail-closed state and cannot distinguish a stale deployment from an unconfigured one. Using them as markers would report staleness that is not there.
